prediction.likelyOutcome: AMT is well-positioned to defeat Pryority's unpaid-rent claim on constructive eviction/breach of the express roof-and-suitability covenant, given the landlord's own admitted decade-long, never-cured leak and the Exhibit A warranty superseding the 'as-is' clause, and to recover a substantial share of its $193,006.35 in documented losses on its counterclaims, net of some discount for AMT's admitted pre-lease knowledge of visible leak damage and the weaker misrepresentation/TCPA overlay theories. The case nets out favorably for the tenant/guarantor on both offense and defense, with a mandatory fee-shifting clause adding further recoverable amounts not yet quantified in this record.

issues.label: Breach of Express Roof-Repair/Suitability Covenant (Exhibit A)

figures.label: AMT's total expenditures in rent, moving, renovation, and other relocation costs
figures.quote: AMT ultimately expended $193,006.35 in rent, moving expenses, renovation expenses, and other costs related to AMT's failed attempt to relocate to the Warehouse.

outcome.description: After a two-day bench trial the court found the landlord materially breached the lease's roof-repair covenant, negligently misrepresented the roof's condition and constructively evicted the tenant, and awarded AMT $193,006.35 in compensatory damages (the full amount it sought for rent, repairs, moving and other expenses) plus $69,002.68 in attorney's fees under the lease; the TCPA claim was denied. The Tennessee Court of Appeals affirmed in its entirety on March 10, 2021.
